title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drains
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee flat on a horizontal drainage line is a widespread mistake that causes frequent clogs. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When used horizontally, the short sweep does not direct waste smoothly along the pipe flow line, leading to solid accumulation and backflow toward upstream fixtures. Proper installation requires a combination Wye and 1/8 bend fitting or a long-turn fitting to maintain fluid momentum and prevent recurring blockages in horizontal drain lines.

Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drains

Installing a standard sanitary tee flat on a horizontal drainage line is a widespread mistake that causes frequent clogs. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When used horizontally, the short sweep does not direct waste smoothly along the pipe flow line, leading to solid accumulation and backflow toward upstream fixtures. Proper installation requires a combination Wye and 1/8 bend fitting or a long-turn fitting to maintain fluid momentum and prevent recurring blockages in horizontal drain lines.
